name: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
title: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
answer: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines cover the practices and tooling that let a quantitative analysis be rerun by someone else, or by the original author later, with the same data, code, environment and results. The scope includes notebook documents that mix code, output and narrative, and the surrounding pipeline that moves data through cleaning, modelling and reporting. It sits inside reproducible work because a notebook alone is rarely enough, the full chain from raw input to final figure must be captured.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines cover the practices and tooling that let a quantitative analysis be rerun by someone else, or by the original author later, with the same data, code, environment and results. The scope includes notebook documents that mix code, output and narrative, and the surrounding pipeline that moves data through cleaning, modelling and reporting. It sits inside reproducible work because a notebook alone is rarely enough, the full chain from raw input to final figure must be captured.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on ordinary research workstations, shared compute clusters and cloud notebook services, with the key requirement being a locked software environment. Common infrastructure includes version control for code and notebooks, container images that pin library versions, and artifact stores for datasets and model outputs. A pipeline runner or workflow manager often sits behind the notebook so that long or scheduled steps do not depend on a human clicking through cells.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method is to treat the notebook as a readable record, not as the execution engine. Analysts write code in small, ordered cells, clear outputs, and keep parameters at the top rather than buried in later cells. The pipeline is then built as a sequence of scripts or tasks that can be run from end to end, with the notebook often generated from those tasks or used only for exploration and presentation. Checksums, data versioning and environment snapshots are recorded at each run.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk and provenance centre on who can see, change and rerun the work, and on whether the results can be trusted. A reproducible pipeline should record where every dataset and model came from, what licence applies, and which version of code produced each output. Risks include leaking credentials or private data inside notebook outputs, silent changes to shared data, and results that cannot be matched to a published claim. Review therefore looks at the full provenance trail, not just the final notebook.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward notebooks that are less like fragile scripts and more like thin views over a robust, versioned pipeline. Expect tighter links between notebook interfaces and workflow systems, automatic capture of environment and data lineage, and better diff and review tools for notebook changes. The goal is that a published result can be regenerated with one command, or at least with a short, documented sequence, years after the original work.
